name: San Marco Platform
tagline: Italian sea platform off Kenya that launched Uhuru, the first satellite dedicated to X-ray astronomy
description: San Marco was a launch platform in the Indian Ocean off Ras Ngomeni, near Malindi, Kenya, about 3 degrees south of the equator, where an eastward launch gets the most help from Earth's rotation. A former oil platform, it was run by the University of Rome's Aerospace Research Centre under a 1962 agreement with NASA; a second platform, Santa Rita, housed launch control, and a smaller one the radar. NASA supplied Scout rockets and trained the Italian crews. San Marco 2 flew from here on 26 April 1967, the first satellite launched from a sea platform. Uhuru, the first satellite dedicated to X-ray astronomy, followed on 12 December 1970 on a Scout B. The last satellite, San Marco D/L, flew in March 1988. ASI has managed the centre since 2004, and its ground station still tracks satellites.
best_known_for: Italian sea platform off Kenya that launched Uhuru, the first satellite dedicated to X-ray astronomy
